questions.q: Which sentence opens a jumbled paragraph: 'The machine then stopped working' or 'A small factory bought a new machine'?
questions.a: The second — 'a machine' introduces the entity; 'the machine' requires it to already exist. A wrong answer shows the student ignores the a→the chain.

questions.q: 'He failed the test.' / 'Ravi never studied.' — which comes first and why?
questions.a: 'Ravi never studied' first — 'He' needs its antecedent 'Ravi' established. Pronoun-before-noun is the reordering giveaway.

questions.q: Order: 'Therefore, the project was cancelled' / 'Funds ran out midway' / 'The project began in 2020'.
questions.a: began (setup) → funds ran out (problem) → therefore cancelled (result). 'Therefore' demands its cause first — connector logic fixes the tail.
